name: Create an organization webhook
description: Create an organization webhook Create a hook that posts payloads in JSON format. POST /orgs/{org}/hooks
context:
POST /orgs/{org}/hooks
Create a hook that posts payloads in JSON format. You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.
Required: org (path) — The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.; body (body)

name: Delete an organization webhook
description: Delete an organization webhook Delete a webhook for an organization. DELETE /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}

name: Get an organization webhook
description: Get an organization webhook Returns a webhook configured in an organization. GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}

name: Get a webhook configuration for an organization
description: Get a webhook configuration for an organization Returns the webhook configuration for an organization. GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/config
context:
GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/config
Returns the webhook configuration for an organization. To get more information about the webhook, including the `active` state and `events`, use "[Get an organization webhook ](/rest/orgs/webhooks#get-an-organization-webhook)." You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.
Required: org (path) — The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.; hook_id (path) — The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

name: Get a webhook delivery for an organization webhook
description: Get a webhook delivery for an organization webhook Returns a delivery for a webhook configured in an organization. GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}

name: List deliveries for an organization webhook
description: List deliveries for an organization webhook Returns a list of webhook deliveries for a webhook configured in an organization. GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries
context:
GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries
Returns a list of webhook deliveries for a webhook configured in an organization. You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.
Required: org (path) — The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.; hook_id (path) — The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.
Optional: per_page (query) — The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."; cursor (query) — Used for pagination: the starting delivery from which the page of deliveries is fetched. Refer to the `link` header for the next and previous page cursors.; status (query) — Returns webhook deliveries filtered by delivery outcome classification based on `status_code` range. A `status` of `success` returns deliveries with a `status_code` in the 200-399 range (inclusive). A `status` of `failure` returns deliveries with a `status_code` in the 400-599 range (inclusive).

name: List organization webhooks
description: List organization webhooks List webhooks for an organization. GET /orgs/{org}/hooks
context:
GET /orgs/{org}/hooks
List webhooks for an organization. The authenticated user must be an organization owner to use this endpoint. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.
Required: org (path) — The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.
Optional: per_page (query) — The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."; page (query) — The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

name: Update an organization webhook
description: Update an organization webhook Updates a webhook configured in an organization. PATCH /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}
context:
PATCH /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}
Updates a webhook configured in an organization. When you update a webhook, the `secret` will be overwritten. If you previously had a `secret` set, you must provide the same `secret` or set a new `secret` or the secret will be removed. If you are only updating individual webhook `config` properties, use "[Update a webhook configuration for an organization](/rest/orgs/webhooks#update-a-webhook-configuration-for-an-organization)". You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.
Required: org (path) — The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.; hook_id (path) — The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.
Optional: body (body)
